cohort: The study included 125 pregnant women attending a tertiary care centre in Midnapore, West Bengal, India.
finding: Asymptomatic bacteriuria was found in 10.4% of pregnant women, with associations identified between ASB and adverse maternal outcomes (anaemia, proteinuria, pyuria, pre-eclampsia, preterm deliveries) and fetal outcomes (low-birth-weight infants, IUGR infants).
mod_finding: The study found no statistically significant difference in operative deliveries between pregnant women with and without asymptomatic bacteriuria.
cross-section timing: Data was collected during pregnancy between October 2022 and September 2023.
